title: Composition of space blowups with controlled centre and strict transforms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subspace whose ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor. For a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$, a morphism $g:Y\to T$, and $p:T^{\prime}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$, the strict transform of $Y$ means the closed subspace of $Y\times_TT^{\prime}$ cut out by the ideal of sections locally annihilated by some power of a local equation of the exceptional effective Cartier divisor $p^{-1}V(\mathcal K)$. Let $T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $\mathcal I_0\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and put $p:T_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_0}T\to T$. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{T_1}$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, and put $q:T_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}T_1\to T_1$. There exist a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ and an isomorphism $e:T_2\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L}T$ over $T$, identifying $pq$ with the blowup map, such that $$|V(\mathcal L)|=|V(\mathcal I_0)|\cup |p|\bigl(|V(\mathcal J)|\bigr).$$ For every algebraic space $Y\to T$, take its strict transform $Y_1\to T_1$ along $p$ and then the strict transform $Y_2\to T_2$ of $Y_1$ along $q$. Under $e$, $Y_2$ is canonically isomorphic to the strict transform of $Y$ along $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L}T\to T$, compatibly with their closed inclusions into $Y\times_TT_2$ and their projections to $Y$ and $T_2$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-blowup-finite-degree-ideal-descent] to $\mathcal I_0$ and $\mathcal J$. The hypotheses are precisely qcqs $T$ and finite-type quasi-coherent ideals on $T$ and $T_1$. Obtain $d>0$ and $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal I_0^d$ of finite type such that $\mathcal H\mathcal O_{T_1}=\mathcal E^d\mathcal J$, where $\mathcal E=\mathcal I_0\mathcal O_{T_1}$. By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], $\mathcal E$ is an effective Cartier ideal.

source.place: Tag 0860 (lemma-composition-finite-type-blowups), finite-degree construction and displayed ideal equality (on the first blowup).

proof.text: Put $R=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal H\mathcal O_{T_1}}T_1$. There are inverse canonical maps $R\leftrightarrows T_2$ over $T_1$, as follows. On $T_2$, the ideals $\mathcal J\mathcal O_{T_2}$ and $\mathcal E\mathcal O_{T_2}$ are effective Cartier: the first by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], the second by [lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup] on scheme charts. Hence their product $\mathcal E^d\mathcal J\mathcal O_{T_2}$ is effective Cartier (locally a product of non-zero-divisors). The universal property [lem-sfb-space-blowup-universal-property] gives $T_2\to R$. Conversely on $R$, $\mathcal E^d\mathcal J\mathcal O_R$ is effective Cartier by the same chart-properties node. On each scheme chart, [lemma-nagata-invertible-product-factor] applied to its factors gives that $\mathcal J\mathcal O_R$ is effective Cartier, yielding $R\to T_2$ by the universal property. Both composites are identities by the uniqueness clause of that property, since their composites to $T_1$ are the structure maps. The use of the two scheme lemmas is legitimate: the chart-properties node identifies these blowups after etale base change with scheme blowups; Cartier regularity is etale local by its definition.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal L=\mathcal I_0\mathcal H$. This is quasi-coherent and finite type: on each affine etale chart the product is generated by the finitely many pairwise products of generators, and [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] computes images and tensor products on charts. Apply [lem-sfb-space-blowup-product-ideal-comparison] to $\mathcal I_0,\mathcal H$. Its second blowup is exactly $R$, so its canonical isomorphism, composed with the preceding $T_2\cong R$, is the required $e:T_2\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L}T$ over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0860 (lemma-composition-finite-type-blowups), second and third paragraphs; Tag 085Y (lemma-blowing-up-two-ideals).

proof.text: Because $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal I_0^d$ and $d>0$, $V(\mathcal I_0)\subseteq V(\mathcal H)$. Off $V(\mathcal I_0)$, [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] identifies $p$ with the identity and $\mathcal E$ with the unit ideal. The equality $\mathcal H\mathcal O_{T_1}=\mathcal E^d\mathcal J$ therefore identifies $V(\mathcal H)$ on this open with $V(\mathcal J)$ on its inverse image. Consequently $|V(\mathcal H)|=|V(\mathcal I_0)|\cup|p|(|V(\mathcal J)|)$. Finally $V(\mathcal I_0\mathcal H)=V(\mathcal I_0)\cup V(\mathcal H)$, checked at a prime on a scheme chart, proves the required support equality for $\mathcal L$.

It remains to compare the two closed subspaces of $Y\times_TT_2$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to T$, then a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to Y\times_TV$. These give a jointly surjective etale cover after every fibre product, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], both blowups over $V$ are ordinary scheme blowups, and $e$ base changes to their composite-blowup isomorphism. The support equality over $V$ follows by repeating step 4 for the restricted ideals: $\mathcal H|_V\subseteq(\mathcal I_0|_V)^d$, the equality on the first blowup restricts to the same equality, and that blowup is the identity off its centre. Apply [lem-sfb-space-strict-transform-etale-locality] first to $p$, then to $q$, and also to the blowup of $\mathcal L$. It identifies the restrictions of the successive transforms with the successive scheme transforms of $U\to V$, and identifies the restriction of the single transform with its scheme transform. On schemes these torsion-convention transforms are those of [def-nagata-strict-transform]: a section is supported on $V(a)$, $a$ a local exceptional equation, iff a power of $a$ kills it, and [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] identifies the supported-section ideal with the closure transform's ideal. So [lem-trf-strict-transform-composition] applies to these schemes, with the pulled-back finite-type ideals and the pulled-back support equality, and identifies the two closed subschemes with their inclusions into $U\times_V(T_2\times_TV)$. Hence their defining ideal sheaves agree on this etale cover. By the closed-subspace/ideal correspondence [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], they agree globally. The resulting canonical isomorphism is the identity of this common closed subspace, so it respects the inclusions and both projections.
